newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU traders present 550,000T wheat deals for Africa.
newsitem.headline: EU traders present 550,000T wheat deals for Africa.

text.p: Grain traders have presented contracts to the European Commission enabling them to export around 550,000 tonnes of wheat to Africa under a special European Union refund scheme, EU grain officials said.

By proving sale of the wheat, traders will qualify for long-term export licences at a refund of 28 Ecus per tonne as part of an EU initiative to offer preferential terms to a group of African countries.
The deadline for showing the contracts was 1500 GMT on Wednesday.
Traders had previously made provisonal applications through France and the Netherlands to export between 330,000 and 941,000 tonnes of wheat.
So-called Article Nine rules require traders to display their contracts following these provisional bids in order to receive the licences which are valid until June 30, 1997.

The 550,000 tonnes or so of confirmed exports bring towards one million tonnes the amount of EU soft wheat earmarked for export to Africa with special subsidies since the start of the July/June grain year.
The officials said this was in line with normal flows of European Union wheat to the countries involved in the scheme, mostly countries with large food deficits.
